rv.q: She is superbly duplicitous in the scene in which she appears to make amends to Jason even as she plans to kill his new wife.
Its textures are a mix of ancient and modern. Though it reverberates with a sense of Greek ritual, there's an acute feeling of up-to-dateness.
The play's tragic force emerges strongly and the production's climax seems better suited to modern tastes than Euripides' original.
Ben Power’s adaptation is admirably clear yet I wonder if it underplays the involvement of the ancient Greeks’ gods and man’s alleged helplessness.
And for us to get to that conclusion is reflective of a quite brilliant production.

cn.t: Critics praise Helen McCrory's commanding, nuanced performance in this modern, disturbing production that humanizes the tragic heroine. Cracknell's direction earns acclaim for its intensity and psychological depth over operatic grandeur.
